A dozen pairs of glowing eyes blink open in the blackness beyond the torchlight, low and many and closing in.
A massive spider the size of a horse descends slowly on a thread from the dark ceiling above the party.
A towering troll-shape looms half-seen in the gloom of the far archway, hunched and breathing and waiting.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the burial alcove, jaw working in silence.
A coiled shadow-serpent shifts in the darkness beneath the floor grating, scales whispering, a single eye catching the light.
Small hunched shapes creep along the tunnel walls in a mass, their yellow eyes blinking, their chatter barely a whisper.
Something long and pale slides from beneath the black water's surface, curling once around the nearest pillar before going still.
A cold mist gathers at the chamber's far end, pulling slowly inward, taking a shape that is almost a figure.
A massive stone form in the alcove has shifted slightly, one arm no longer where it was a moment ago.
The ceiling erupts in a shrieking black wave of wings, leathery and frantic, blotting the torchlight entirely for a terrible moment.
Something enormous breathes in the dark beyond the pillars, and the shadow it casts has horns and the weight of a wall.
The iron-bound chest in the center of the room has no lock, and it just moved, just slightly, toward the door.
A robed figure sits motionless on a throne of black stone far ahead, eye sockets faintly luminous, watching without blinking.
A pale hand the length of a forearm grips the dungeon's ceiling crack overhead, then a second hand reaches and grips again.
In the collapsed corridor, two burning amber eyes float at chest height, unblinking, attached to nothing the torchlight can quite reach.
The dungeon pool bulges upward as something vast and formless shifts beneath, and the ripples move outward like a slow warning.
A figure stands just inside the far doorway, translucent and still, wearing armor that rusted to dust three centuries ago.
The iron portcullis bends inward with a slow groan, something on the other side pressing calmly through the bars without hurry.
Fungal growths along the wall pulse with a faint bioluminescence, and the largest cluster has begun to slowly lean toward the party.
A humanoid shape clings flat against the ceiling above the treasure pile, perfectly motionless, watching with lidless eyes as the party enters.
From the pit's depths below the rope bridge, something enormous inhales, and the torches gutter sideways all at once toward the hole.
The dungeon wall itself ripples, a massive worm-shape pressing outward from within the stone, then stilling, as if reconsidering its moment.
A wolf-sized rat crouches at the tunnel's edge, enormous and unafraid, regarding the party with an intelligence that has no business there.
The hanging chains in the torture chamber sway despite no wind, and a low sound rises that is not quite a voice.
Far down the corridor, a silhouette stands where the map shows no room, no door, no passage, nothing that should be there.
A towering troll-shape looms half-seen in the gloom of the far archway, hunched and breathing heavily.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the crypt floor, eye sockets flickering faintly.
Something long and scaled coils and uncoils just beyond the light, patient, watching, tasting the air.
Small shadows pour silently through the cracks in the far wall, dozens of them, whispering in a guttural tongue.
A pale tentacle thicker than a man's thigh slides from the black water and rests along the dock's edge.
The mist at the corridor's end thickens and pulls inward, assuming something like shoulders, something like a face.
Deep within the alcove, two great stone eyes grind slowly open, and the grinding does not stop there.
The ceiling explodes outward in a shrieking black wave, leather wings and claws filling every inch of torchlit air.
In the chamber beyond the portcullis, something enormous turns, and the horned silhouette fills the entire doorframe.
The chest in the corner shifts almost imperceptibly, its latch splitting into teeth, its hinges bending like knuckles.
Atop the far throne, a robed figure sits perfectly still, its hollow gaze finding you before the torch reaches it.
A rust-red claw curls slowly around the pillar's edge and then withdraws without a sound.
Shapes move beneath the mosaic floor's cracked surface, pressing upward, too many, too deliberate to be shadows.
Something with far too many legs skitters across the wall above the doorway and vanishes before the lantern swings up.
A low moan fills the passage and a pale figure drifts through the solid stone wall, trailing cold behind it.
The armor standing in the corner was not there a moment ago, and its visor turns very slowly toward you.
Far down the flooded hall, a single enormous eye opens beneath the surface and locks onto the torchlight.
The gargoyle perched above the gate has shifted position since you passed beneath it the first time.
Something whispers your name from inside the sealed sarcophagus, and then the lid begins to move from within.
A wolf-sized rat freezes at the corridor's edge, staring, then retreats into the dark to report to something larger.
Black smoke pours from the sconces and thickens into a shape with hands that reach toward the nearest throat.
The shadow cast by nothing stretches long across the dungeon floor, moving against the direction of every light source.
In the pit below the grate, something breathes, slow and massive, and one scaled eyelid rises toward the glow.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the far corner, eyesockets burning pale.
A coiled shadow-serpent thicker than a man's torso shifts in the darkness beneath the bridge, scales whispering against wet rock.
Small hunched shapes creep between pillars, dozens of them, red eyes blinking in and out of the torchlight's edge.
A pale tentacle as thick as a forearm slides silently from the black water beside the dock and feels across the stone.
Cold mist pools near the ceiling and begins to thicken, pulling inward, taking the rough suggestion of a reaching shape.
Deep within a collapsed archway, two enormous stone eyes grind open, and something massive and grey begins to shift forward.
The entire far wall suddenly explodes into a shrieking black cloud, leathery wings and small claws filling every inch of air.
In the far passage, a horned silhouette stands motionless, head lowered, shoulders broad as a cart, knuckles dragging the floor.
The ornate chest in the corner exhales slowly, its latch flexing, its wood grain rippling in a way wood should never move.
On a distant obsidian throne, a robed figure sits perfectly still, its hollow gaze tracking every movement without ever shifting.
Something enormous presses against the iron gate, bending the bars outward slowly, deliberately, as though testing whether they will hold.
A long segmented shape clings to the ceiling, motionless until the torchlight catches dozens of legs and two curving black pincers.
The portrait on the wall has turned. It was facing left a moment ago, and now the painted eyes are watching you directly.
Three feet of curved yellow claw scrape around the dungeon corner, and then pause, as though whatever owns them is listening.
A luminous jellyfish shape drifts through the wall itself, translucent and vast, trailing tendrils that pass through the stone floor silently.
Something beneath the flagstones pushes upward rhythmically, cracking grout, and a black clawed hand breaks through and reaches blindly upward.
A wolf the height of a pony stands at the tunnel mouth, fur silver-grey and eyes molten gold, entirely motionless.
The darkness in the alcove is wrong, too thick, too still, and it shifts slightly when no draft is present to move it.
A humanoid figure stands submerged in the flooded chamber, just beneath the surface, open eyes staring upward at the ceiling without blinking.
From deep within the collapsed rubble something ancient and scaled exhales, and the dust on the floor rolls outward in a slow ring.
Iron chains scrape the floor slowly, pulled by something unseen moving through the furthest shadows, steady and purposeful and unhurried.
Two amber eyes the size of dinner plates open in the ceiling high above, and a breath like a forge bellows down.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the floor, hollow sockets turning toward the light.
A coiled shadow-serpent thick as a man's torso shifts silently in the darkness beneath the far wall, scales whispering.
Small hunched shapes creep through the cracks and low passages, dozens of goblin eyes glinting just beyond the torch's reach.
A pale tentacle as thick as a log slides soundlessly from the black water at the dungeon's edge, feeling, searching.
Mist pools and thickens near the broken sarcophagus, gathering shape, two hollow points of cold light forming where eyes should be.
A vast stone figure in the corner has shifted position since the party entered, though no one saw it move.
The ceiling explodes with frantic wings and chittering darkness as a swarm of bats pours downward like a living black wave.
A silhouette broad as a doorway fills the tunnel ahead, horned and massive, the slow snort of breath echoing toward you.
The iron-bound chest in the corner sits perfectly still, but the keyhole blinks once, slowly, in the dark.
On the obsidian throne across the chamber sits a robed figure, motionless, crowned, watching with eyes that glow like dying embers.
A shape that is almost a man but too tall and too thin stands unmoving in the flooded passage, ankle-deep in black water.
Something with too many legs moves through the stalactites overhead, pausing when the torchlight swings up, vanishing before it can be seen clearly.
The shadows behind the pillars pool and writhe, thickening into a shape with shoulders and reaching arms that stretch and shrink.
Low guttural breathing comes from the sealed alcove, rhythmic and slow, accompanied by the creak of something very large shifting its weight.
A pair of rust-red eyes opens in the far wall at roughly the height of a standing man, unblinking, watching.
The corpse at the base of the stairs has been moved since the party last passed, now facing the corridor, hands folded.
Chains rattle deep in the pit below the grating, the sound climbing closer, something hauling itself up hand over iron hand.
A shape writhes behind the cracked dungeon door, visible only as writhing darkness through the gap, pressing, waiting to be let through.
The water in the underground channel ripples against the current in long, slow waves, as though something enormous breathes beneath the surface.
An armored figure stands motionless in the alcove, visor down, but the gauntleted hand has moved since the last time anyone looked.
At the far edge of the torchlight, a hunched shape covered in matted fur watches from all fours, teeth barely visible.
The darkness at the passage's end does not behave like darkness, thickening and shifting, swallowing light that should reach it but does not.
Bones scrape stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the shadows at the chamber's edge, hollow sockets fixed forward.
Something vast and coiled shifts in the darkness below, scales catching no light, a forked tongue tasting the air.
Small shapes shuffle and whisper in the passage beyond, dozens of them, creeping forward on clawed feet just outside the torch's reach.
A pale tentacle thicker than a man's thigh slides silently over the lip of the flooded channel, feeling ahead of it.
Cold mist pools low across the floor and thickens at the far wall, taking a shape that nearly resembles shoulders and hollow eyes.
Deep in the alcove, stone grinds against stone; something massive and broad shifts its weight and slowly turns its featureless face toward the light.
The ceiling explodes inward as a black shrieking wave of wings and teeth pours down from a crack no one noticed.
In the archway ahead, something huge and horned breathes slowly in the dark, the silhouette of a massive head lowering with patience.
The chest in the corner hasn't moved, but its latch is slightly open now, and something glistens faintly along the seam.
Upon a throne of crumbled bone at the chamber's far end, a hooded figure sits perfectly still and watches without blinking.
Across the water, a pair of amber eyes hover motionless at surface level, patient and enormous and not yet moving.
A shape hangs upside-down from the far archway, long arms nearly brushing the floor, its breath a low and rhythmic rasp.
The shadow on the wall behind you does not match anyone standing in the room.
Something shifts under the loose flagstones ahead, pressing upward slowly, the stones bulging and cracking with quiet, deliberate force.
A smell of rot arrives before the shape does, a hulking darkness filling the corridor, dragging something behind it with wet sounds.
Far down the flooded passage, a pale humanoid form drifts upright just beneath the surface, drifting slowly and steadily toward the light.
In the pit below the broken grate, a dozen grey hands grip the edges, and more are appearing.
A column in the chamber moves. Just once. Then stands still again, breathing.
Silk-thin threads cross the doorway ahead, freshly strung, and something stirs in the high corner above them, alert and many-eyed.
The torch flame bends toward the passage on the left, and from that darkness comes a sound like slow wings folding closed.
One of the statues lining the corridor is now facing a different direction than it was a moment ago.
A long thin shadow pools across the ceiling and stretches toward the party from above, cast by nothing visible below it.
Ancient bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the dust, eye sockets igniting with cold fire.
Something vast and serpentine coils in the shadows along the wall, scales whispering against wet stone with each slow breath.
Dozens of small hunched shapes creep forward in the dark, yellow eyes blinking, claws ticking softly across the dungeon floor.
A pale tentacle as thick as a man's thigh slides silently over the edge of the flooded passage, feeling blindly ahead.
The mist in the far corner thickens, pulls inward, and slowly assembles itself into something that almost has a face.
Deep in the alcove, a massive shape of cracked stone groans and shifts, shedding dust as it begins to stand.
The ceiling explodes into motion, a shrieking black torrent of wings and teeth pouring down from somewhere far above.
Enormous curved horns catch the torchlight in the passage ahead, and the floor shudders beneath a weight that is still approaching.
The ornate chest in the corner has too many teeth along its lid, and its brass hinges are slowly opening.
On a throne of crumbling bone at the chamber's far end, a withered figure sits perfectly still, watching with hollow burning eyes.
Something with too many legs skitters across the ceiling just beyond the light, pausing only when the party stops moving.
A long-fingered hand grips the far doorframe from below, pale and boneless-looking, followed by a head that tilts at an impossible angle.
Ripples spread outward across the black water of the underground pool, slow and deliberate, something circling just beneath the surface.
The shadow on the wall does not match any shape in the room, and it is moving against the torchlight's direction.
A low grinding rumble fills the passage as two enormous stone doors ahead part slightly, something immense pressing through from the other side.
In the collapsed hall beyond, dozens of pale shapes huddle motionless until one slowly raises a jawless head toward the party.
Twin phosphorescent lights drift at shoulder height in the flooded lower chamber, unblinking, separated by the width of a very large skull.
The iron portcullis above rattles once, and something grips the bars from the other side, knuckles white and terribly large.
A low hissing fills the room from every direction at once, and a smell like cold ash and rotting flowers thickens the air.
Chains rattle deep in the darkness ahead, growing louder, then stopping — and something in the black begins to breathe in ragged bursts.
The carved stone face on the dungeon wall has changed position since the party last looked, and its mouth is now open.
Fungal light pulses faintly in the cavern below, illuminating for just a moment a silhouette far too large to fit the passage ahead.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the tomb floor, hollow eye sockets filling with pale light.
Small clawed hands and glinting yellow eyes multiply at the tunnel's edge as the goblin horde inches silently forward.
A pale tentacle, slick and ridged, slides over the lip of the flooded chamber floor, feeling blindly toward the light.
A wraith coalesces from the drifting mist near the far wall, barely a shape, barely a sound, barely there yet.
Deep grinding fills the corridor as a massive stone figure slowly unclenches its fists in the alcove you nearly walked past.
The ceiling erupts in a shrieking black torrent of bats, pouring from some unseen roost directly overhead and downward.
A silhouette broad as a cart and crowned with curving horns stands motionless in the smoke beyond the broken portcullis.
The treasure chest in the corner has too many hinges, and something wet glistens along its slowly parting seam.
On a throne of black iron at the chamber's far end, a robed figure sits perfectly still, watching with eyes that glow faintly violet.
A gelatinous mass presses silently through the low passage behind you, smothering the torchlight one guttering inch at a time.
The shadow on the cavern wall moves against the torchlight, spreading wide dark wings that belong to nothing visible nearby.
Dozens of tiny red points of light swarm along the floor in the darkness, skittering and chittering just beyond the firelight.
A long-fingered hand grips the top of the pit's edge, knuckles pale, nails black, and does not yet pull itself up.
Something enormous rolls slowly in the underground lake, briefly surfacing a ridge of dark, armored hide before slipping silently below.
The wolf-shaped darkness at the tunnel mouth does not move, does not breathe, only watches with eyes like two cold embers.
Chains rattle deep in the far cell block and something very large tests its restraints slowly, methodically, with growing force.
A figure shaped like a hanged man sways from the rafters in perfect stillness, then turns its head toward your torchlight.
The mold covering the dungeon wall pulses faintly, rhythmically, spreading tendrils toward the nearest sleeping adventurer in near-perfect silence.
An enormous claw-tip scrapes a single long groove into the stone floor just past the threshold, then withdraws into total darkness.
The pile of discarded armor in the corner breathes, its helm slowly turning until two dim red points of light find you.
From somewhere deep below the grate you stand on, something ancient exhales, and the warm fetid breath rises through the iron gaps.
Bones scrape stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the floor, hollow sockets turning slowly toward the light.
Something vast and serpentine coils in the corner shadows, scales whispering against the floor, a forked tongue tasting the air.
Small hunched shapes creep along the walls, dozens of them, their yellow eyes multiplying as they edge closer through the dark.
A pale tentacle as thick as a man's thigh slides silently from the black water, feeling blindly across the wet stone.
Mist pools near the far wall begin to thicken and rise, slowly assembling a shape with hollow eyes and reaching arms.
Deep in the alcove, carved stone eyelids grind open, and a massive granite figure shifts its enormous weight forward with a groan.
The ceiling erupts in a shrieking black wave, a thousand leathery wings and tiny claws pouring downward out of the dark above.
A silhouette broader than any doorway stands motionless at the corridor's end, two curved horns scraping the ceiling as it breathes.
The large ornate chest in the corner has not moved, but its lid has shifted slightly, and something glints wetly within.
Upon a throne of crumbling bone, a robed figure sits utterly still, two violet pinpricks of light watching from beneath a deep hood.
Ripples spread without source across the flooded chamber floor, and below the surface something long and dark circles slowly beneath your feet.
A hand, gray and long-fingered, curls around the edge of the broken doorframe and tightens, pulling a hidden shape into half-view.
From the pit in the chamber's center comes a low rhythmic scraping, growing louder, and two enormous claws appear at the rim.
Shadows on the far wall move opposite the torchlight, forming the unmistakable outline of great folded wings pressing slowly open.
The statue at the corridor's end is facing the wrong direction, and one of its stone hands has descended to grip a sword.
Something breathes behind the tapestry, slow and heavy, and the ancient fabric billows outward with each exhale toward the party.
Eyes like twin embers float in the rafters above, unblinking, surrounded by a vague darkness that drinks the torchlight around it.
From the collapsed wall, a mass of scuttling chitinous legs emerges, filling the breach, pouring forward like a tide of clicking shadow.
The iron portcullis on the far side has begun to rise on its own, and in the blackness beyond, something large shifts its weight.
A shape detaches from the dungeon wall itself, tall and thin and wrong, stepping forward on too many joints, head tilting silently.
The surface of the dark mirror across the chamber reflects the room accurately except for one addition: a vast shape standing behind you.
Chains rattle deep in the flooded passage, and two enormous pale hands grip the submerged archway, pulling something enormous slowly through.
Bones scrape against stone as a skeletal guardian drags itself upright from the floor, eye sockets kindling with pale fire.
Something coils in the shadow beside the pillar, slow and vast, scaled and patient, its tongue tasting the air.
Small shapes creep along the walls in numbers too great to count, yellow eyes catching the torchlight for just a moment.
A pale tentacle slides silently from the black water at the dungeon's edge, feeling across the wet stone toward dry land.
The mist near the far wall thickens, darkens, and begins to take the shape of something with arms and hollow eyes.
Deep beneath the rubble, two enormous stone fists slowly unclench, and a grinding groan fills the entire chamber with dread.
The darkness above explodes with the shriek of a thousand wings, a roiling black mass dropping fast toward the torchlight.
In the passage beyond, a shape fills the entire width of the corridor, horned and broad and snorting in the dark.
The chest in the corner has no keyhole, and as you watch, its lid shifts open just a fraction too slowly.
On the obsidian throne across the hall, a robed figure sits perfectly still, and its hollow gaze has not blinked once.
Thin fingers curl around the dungeon door's edge from the other side, too long, too many joints, withdrawing without a sound.
A low rumble trembles up through the floor as something enormous moves just beyond the collapsed tunnel, dislodging ancient stone.
The surface of the underground lake ripples outward from a central point, though nothing visible has broken the surface yet.
Something wraps itself around the far stalactite, hanging upside down, too large to be a bat, watching with lidless eyes.
The torchlight flickers as a cold wind comes from nowhere, and briefly illuminates a gaunt figure standing just behind the last soldier.
Chains rattle in the darkness of the pit below the grate, and then fall silent, and then rattle again, closer now.
A door at the far end of the corridor swings open on its own, and beyond it is only total, breathing darkness.
Something with too many legs skitters across the ceiling faster than the torchlight can follow, scattering dust down onto upturned faces.
The armor standing in the alcove was not facing that direction when the party first passed it minutes ago.
A low, wet gurgling rises from the drain in the floor, and the iron grate begins to bulge upward from below.
Shadows peel away from the wall and gather into a tall, featureless figure that simply stands at the corridor's end, watching.
